source.title: Referential communication in heterogeneous communities of pre-trained visual deep networks
source.authors: Mat'eo Mahaut; Roberto Dessì; Francesca Franzon; M. Baroni

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present, including appendices. The text gives the published venue as Transactions on Machine Learning Research (04/2025), despite the supplied venue field.
record.tranche_reason: Tests cross-model interoperability using a learned communication interface and message-space comparisons, rather than directly measuring raw representation similarity or scale trends.
record.gate_note: The paper trains communication layers on purpose, so successful communication is evidence that a learned interface can connect these models, not that their untreated representations spontaneously converge. The paper also reports a nonsignificant relationship between pretrained representation similarity and communication performance; that finding is recorded under fits_no_version because it is not itself a test of scale convergence or a mapping result.
record.test_reason: The study freezes heterogeneous pre-trained vision networks and trains light linear interface layers into a shared message space. It compares heterogeneous with same-architecture pairs and tests classifier transfer across senders. This is a learned-mapping test of whether different models' representations are interchangeable (V4), not a direct similarity or scale measurement.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that frozen heterogeneous vision networks, with light trained interface layers, develop a shared referential protocol. They say this suggests the networks already converged to similar representations, that new agents learn the protocol quickly, and that it supports classifier transfer. They also report that the protocol generalizes only partially out of domain, with notable drops for heterogeneous pairs. They also find that RSA similarity does not predict communication success.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains task-specific communication layers and measures referential-game success, message distances, and classifier transfer; it does not use the original sources' direct representation-similarity or convergence methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports different message dimensions (16 and 64), and message-distance results differ between independently trained one-to-one pairs and jointly trained populations.

fits_no_version.finding: RSA similarity of pre-trained visual-module outputs was not significantly correlated with communication accuracy or learning time.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Raw representational similarity between vision models does not predict how easily a learned interface connects them.

fits_no_version.finding: Senders trained jointly in a population converge on near-identical messages for the same image; independently trained one-to-one senders do not.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Shared learned protocols arise from joint training, not from pre-existing representational identity.

record.code_released: https://github.com/mahautm/emecom_pop_data (dataset reproduction scripts); experiment scripts are stated to be in ./egg/zoo/pop, with no URL given for that path.
record.peer_reviewed: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (04/2025); reviewed on OpenReview.
record.problems: Communication interfaces are deliberately trained, so the results do not establish spontaneous alignment of untouched representations. The study does not test scaling with model size or capability. The population protocol is jointly trained; independently trained one-to-one senders do not show the same message-level convergence. Message-distance values in Figure 5 are presented graphically without numerical values in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Did not extract referential-accuracy results for generalization to single-class, OOD, and other datasets, or perturbation and discrete-channel experiments: these assess downstream communication robustness rather than directly measuring cross-model representation alignment. Table 3, Table 4, Table 5, Table 20, Figure 4, and Appendix C.

untested.parts: No sweep over model size or capability, and no alignment-versus-scale trend.
No image-caption paired representation comparison. CLIP is used only as an image encoder.
No same-architecture, different-seed comparison of features or subspaces.
No fixed post-hoc linear map between raw representations, no intermediate-layer stitching, and no unpaired mapping. Interfaces are trained jointly on a contrastive task.
SAE features are examined for one sender-receiver pair only. Feature recurrence across models is not tested.
No dependence of a similarity metric on its settings or inputs is tested.
No test of shared data or objectives as the cause of alignment.

missing.what: Heterogeneous vs homogeneous accuracy on single-class, OOD, Cifar100, Places205 and CelebA sets (large heterogeneous drop off-domain). rows_left_out excluded these, but they bear directly on V4's 'little loss'.
No-interface baseline: label-matching between heterogeneous pretrained models gives 58.3% on ImageNet val and 16.1% on OOD.
New heterogeneous learner agents reach at least 90% accuracy (64-d) when learning an existing protocol; unseen models (LeViT, CaiT, ResNeXt, DenseNet) exceed 95% from epoch 1; CLIP shows no drop.
missing.locator: Section 4.3, Fig. 2, Appendix M Fig. 9, Appendix N

missing.what: Per-pair accuracy matrix: the lowest pairs are ResNet-COCO with ViT-B or DINO, differing in both architecture and pretraining corpus.

record.verdict_notes: V4 evidence rests on jointly trained interfaces (a linear sender layer and a two-layer receiver) with a contrastive objective, so this is a weaker form of interchangeability than a fixed post-hoc map. The homogeneous rows (r1, r4) and same-sender classifier rows are baselines, not V4 evidence. The rows_left_out rationale is mistaken: the OOD tables are the clearest qualifier of V4 in this paper.

versions.untested_parts: No scale sweep or comparison of representational alignment against model size or capability.
No paired image-and-caption representations are compared. CLIP is used as an image encoder, not as a vision-language alignment test.
No study of same-architecture models trained from different initializations learning shared features or subspaces.
The interfaces are trained for referential communication; the paper does not test stitching intermediate layers, unpaired mapping, or mapping with no task-specific training.
SAE features are inspected for one sender-receiver example, but recurrence of the same features or circuits across different models is not tested.
Input perturbations and dataset transfer are evaluated for communication accuracy, not for dependence of a representation-similarity estimate on its metric, settings, or inputs.
The study does not determine whether shared training data or objectives, rather than a common model of reality, explain representational alignment.

relationships.condition: In-domain ImageNet1k referential game, 16- and 64-d messages; population classifier transfer on OOD classes
relationships.reason: Heterogeneous pairs nearly match homogeneous pairs (95.3 vs 99.3; 99.2 vs 98.6). Population pairs reach 96.8/98.2. Transferred classifiers stay near or above same-sender accuracy (r2, r3, r5, r6, r11, r13, r15, r17, r19, r21, r23).
relationships.display_finding: Heterogeneous pairs scored 95.3 versus 99.3 and 99.2 versus 98.6 for homogeneous pairs, population pairs reached 96.8/98.2, and transferred classifiers stayed near or above same-sender accuracy.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot transfer of the learned interface to out-of-domain classes and other datasets (Tables 3-5, 20)
relationships.reason: Based on text, not rows: off-domain, heterogeneous pairs fall far below homogeneous ones. Examples: OOD 62.9 vs 90.5 (64-d), Cifar100 25.8 vs 80.5, CelebA 48.1 vs 98.1. Cross-model mappability degrades outside the training distribution. No rows capture this.
relationships.display_finding: Heterogeneous pairs trailed homogeneous pairs at 62.9 versus 90.5 on out-of-domain classes, 25.8 versus 80.5 on CIFAR100, and 48.1 versus 98.1 on CelebA.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Heterogeneous pairs and population training on the in-domain referential game
reader_labels.reason: Learned interfaces yielded high test accuracy across heterogeneous pairings and population pairings; the shared population protocol also transferred classifiers across senders (r2, r3, r5, r6, r11, r13, r17, r19, r21, r23).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Separately trained one-to-one protocols versus the jointly trained population protocol
reader_labels.reason: Messages from independently trained one-to-one senders were much less similar for the same images and near the different-image reference, unlike the population senders’ shared messages (r7-r9).
